title: NATO/FMN-first security-label conformance linter, releasability-derivation simulator and coalition-format adapter kit (STANAG 4774/4778, ACP-240/ZTDF, NFFI/NVG/MIP) built on public standards and synthetic data
problem: Allied C2 vendors and national test cells discover STANAG 4774/4778 label, ACP-240/ZTDF and NFFI/NVG/MIP conformance defects late (mostly at the annual CWIX), and coalition staffs still hand-tag or regenerate products, yet no vendor-neutral, unclassified tool lets a producer lint labels, simulate the releasability a partner would derive, and emit conformant coalition formats before data leaves a national system.

user.exact_role: Interoperability/conformance engineer at an allied C2 or messaging vendor preparing an FMN spiral capability for CWIX; secondarily the NATO ACT/JFTC test director, an NCIA data-centric-security (DCS) IV&V engineer, and a national CWIX cell (e.g., Bundeswehr) - the FDO/JICO hand-tagger is the downstream beneficiary, not the tool user
user.echelon: Vendor / national test cell / NATO agency (enterprise and exercise), not tactical
organization_examples: NATO ACT Federated Interoperability branch / JFTC CWIX
U.S. Joint Staff J6 JDAT / Bold Quest (ACP-240 as coalition testing standard)

current_workflow: Vendor implements the FMN spiral profile (labels per ADatP-4774/4778 with a SPIF per ADatP-5636; NFFI/NVG/MIP/ADatP-3 exchanges) from NATO standards, some of which are NATO RESTRICTED
Vendor self-tests with in-house scripts, Isode/Fortra-class label libraries or the open-source Spiffing library; some hire CWIX-preparation consultancies (Corvus, Thalorin, Mility)

Nation registers the capability for CWIX; three weeks in June the capability is tested against other nations' live systems; INSPECT (NATO ACT's near-fielded continuous conformance platform) is meant to run automated checks year-round
Failures are logged; fixes deferred to the next spiral/CWIX; compliance registry updated
In operations and exercises, releasability of objects that were never labelled at source is decided by FDOs/JICOs by hand (WFX 24-03, Balikatan 2026) or products are regenerated on the REL enclave
current_solution: Vendor label libraries and products (Isode, Fortra Data Classification/Titus-Boldon James, archTIS NC Protect, Janusnet, Nexor), the open-source Spiffing SPIF/label/clearance library (Surevine), NATO ACT's CWIX and INSPECT, NCIA's own IV&V bundled into DCS COTS procurements, OGC/AWS DCS reference implementations, and CWIX-preparation consultancies (Corvus Intelligence, Thalorin, Mility). On the FVEY/U.S. side the ACP-240/ZTDF wrapper is Virtru/OpenTDF paired with Everfox guards; there is no public conformance linter for ACP-240 and Joint Staff J6 tests it at Bold Quest.
failure: Conformance is checked late and by the parties that own the registry (NATO ACT via CWIX/INSPECT) or bundled into COTS IV&V (NCIA DCS), so a third-party linter has no owner; the releasability that a partner will actually derive from a label plus SPIF plus its clearance is opaque to producers, but the ground truth needed to validate a derivation simulator (national SPIFs, REL decisions) is restricted; and the adapter kit half competes with SitaWare's native multi-standard support and government-owned TAK federation.

evidence.claim: NCIA issued RFQ-CO-424368-DCS 'Data Centric Security Milestone 1 - Basic Labelling' to procure a COTS labelling tool for informal email and Office documents, perform COTS adaptation plus independent verification and validation (including security validation) against ADatP-4774, ADatP-4778 and ADatP-5636, and specify a Metadata Binding Service API for FMN Spiral 4 core and collaboration services; value reported by a third-party aggregator as about EUR 1.6M with a 23 July 2026 deadline
evidence.source_title: NCIA current opportunity 424368 (Data Centric Security Milestone 1 - Basic Labelling) and hermix.com summary
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CWIX25 ran more than 25,000 tests on about 600 capabilities from 40 nations and NATO ACT described INSPECT as a near-fielded platform for continuous automated conformance checks (24/7/365) to expose defects earlier
evidence.source_title: CWIX25 Delivers Digital Interoperability for NATO & Nations - NATO ACT
evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: They have, in the only forms the market pays for: (1) label syntax/binding libraries and products are sold by Isode, Fortra, archTIS, Janusnet and Nexor, several with a decade of CWIX participation; (2) the open-source Spiffing library already provides a free SPIF/label/clearance engine; (3) year-round conformance is owned by NATO ACT (INSPECT) and CWIX, and NCIA bundles IV&V into its DCS COTS procurement (RFQ-CO-424368-DCS) rather than buying a separate linter; (4) the compliance-tooling and CWIX-preparation layer is already served by small consultancies (Thalorin, Corvus, Mility) - which is exactly the consultancy-shaped end state this gap would converge to. What no one sells is a producer-side releasability-derivation simulator for machine-generated tactical objects, but validating one requires national SPIFs and real REL decisions that are restricted, and the buyer for that (U.S. MPE/NGC2, NCIA later DCS milestones) either killed the parent gaps or has not tendered it.
technical_wedge: An open-source, deterministic toolkit: (a) a STANAG 4774/4778 + ADatP-5636 SPIF linter (XML and JSON/JOSE encodings) that validates syntax, binding signatures, SPIF consistency and FMN spiral profile constraints and produces a machine-readable report; (b) an ACP-240/ZTDF assertion checker built on the public OpenTDF spec; (c) a 'would-this-pass' releasability simulator that, given a label, a synthetic SPIF and a synthetic partner clearance matrix, shows which partner enclaves would derive access and where dominance/NOFORN-style rules block aggregation; (d) NFFI/NVG/MIP-JC3IEDM and CoT export adapters with schema validation; packaged as a CI job vendors run before CWIX and as a demo at TIDE Hackathon / CWIX Innovation Sandbox. It is buildable, but nothing in it is proprietary.

mvp.what: Command-line and web linter for STANAG 4774/4778 labels and SPIFs with an ACP-240/ZTDF assertion checker, a releasability-derivation simulator on synthetic SPIFs/clearances, and CoT-to-NFFI/NVG exporters with regression dashboard
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes - 2-4 months for one engineer using public STANAG/ADatP texts, the OpenTDF spec and the Spiffing test corpus; the constraint is getting a CWIX/TIDE slot (annual) or a vendor willing to run it, not the build
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That it catches label/binding/SPIF and coalition-format regressions a vendor would otherwise discover at CWIX, in minutes rather than at the June event; that its simulated derivations agree with a reference implementation (Isode/Spiffing) on a shared synthetic corpus; and that at least one vendor or national cell values this enough to pay

data_requirement.what: Standards texts (STANAG/ADatP-4774, 4778, 5636; ACP-240 and OpenTDF/ZTDF spec; NFFI, NVG, MIP/JC3IEDM and ADatP-3 schemas), FMN spiral profiles and test cases, sample labelled objects and SPIFs
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Partly. ADatP-4774/4778/5636 and the OpenTDF spec are public; NFFI/NVG/MIP schemas and the Spiffing test data are public; FMN spiral specifications, CWIX test cases and national SPIFs are partly NATO RESTRICTED or nation-controlled and would need a national sponsor - access for the Indonesian co-founder is not assured and needs sponsor/counsel clarification; real REL decisions (ground truth for the simulator) are not obtainable and would be replaced by synthetic data by construction

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: U.S. SBIR/STTR is irrelevant (no U.S. buyer) and would in any case require majority U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership and control. A German GmbH can enter DIANA and NATO channels; DIANA and NATO Innovation Fund ownership/control tests and NCIA's BOA plus national Declaration of Eligibility require counsel and a sponsoring nation - the Indonesian co-founder's equity share and access to NATO RESTRICTED spiral material are the open questions. No ITAR exposure for NATO-origin public standards work; German export rules (AWG/AWV, EU dual-use) can apply to software with military end use - needs counsel. The 2026 DIANA deadline (3 July 2026) and the NCIA DCS MS1 deadline (23 July 2026) have already passed.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, trivially, and the relevant incumbents are smaller than those: Isode, Fortra or archTIS can publish a linter in a quarter from their existing libraries; Systematic already self-certifies; NATO ACT is building INSPECT; Virtru controls the ZTDF reference implementation. Anduril/Palantir do not need to respond because the product does not touch their revenue.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a company. The only positioning available is 'neutral open-source reference linter', which is a credential rather than a business; there is no data, integration, accreditation or network asset a startup accumulates that an incumbent or NATO itself lacks.

capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: 120,000-250,000 (TIDE Hackathon / CWIX Innovation Sandbox participation, travel, a NATO-nation sponsor relationship, a restricted-material-cleared hire or subcontractor for FMN spiral profiles)

capital_required.assumptions: Two founders on minimal salary; no classified facility; sponsor grants restricted-material access; revenue per customer EUR 20-100k for pilots - hence the venture-scale question is not answered by capital but by market size

expertise_required.why: The linter and binding checks are schema/signature validation; the founding engineer covers this

expertise_required.role: NATO DCS/FMN practitioner with CWIX or NCIA DCS experience (ideally ex-Isode/NCIA/national cell)
expertise_required.why: Knows spiral profiles, SPIF practice, INSPECT status and who at ACT/NCIA/vendors decides; without them the team cannot get a CWIX slot or a pilot

expertise_required.why: Access to restricted spiral material and Innovation Sandbox nomination run through nations
Cap table for DIANA/NIF, NCIA BOA eligibility, dual-use export rules and the non-NATO-national co-founder's access

regulatory_burden.explanation: Public NATO standards and synthetic data carry no ITAR/EAR technical-data burden; no ATO, CDS accreditation or clearance is required for the tool itself. Burden appears only when the team needs NATO RESTRICTED spiral profiles or CWIX test cases (nation-controlled) or wants an NCIA contract (BOA plus national Declaration of Eligibility, security clearances for staff on some RFQs). German export rules for military-end-use software need counsel.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian co-founder can lawfully work on everything built from public standards and synthetic data. Constraints to describe, not judge: NATO RESTRICTED material is released per nation and a non-NATO national's access is not assured; DIANA/NIF and NCIA eligibility tests look at ownership and control and may require the German founder to hold majority control; U.S. SBIR is closed to this cap table. All need counsel.

dual_use_potential.explanation: NATO confidentiality labels, SPIFs, ACP-240 and NFFI/NVG/MIP have no commercial analogue; the nearest commercial adjacency (enterprise data classification) is already served by Fortra/Microsoft Purview. Only the generic 'schema conformance CI' pattern is reusable, and it is not a business.

defensibility.explanation: Nothing durable. The standards are public, the data is synthetic by design, the reference engine is open source (Spiffing), the authoritative harness is government-owned (INSPECT/CWIX) and the ACP-240 reference implementation is Virtru/OpenTDF. At best the team accumulates a curated synthetic regression corpus and relationships at ACT/NCIA/vendors - the assets of a consultancy.

why_now: FMN Spiral 4 became mandatory for missions 2025-2027 and Spiral 5 is in development; NCIA started procuring DCS labelling in 2026 (Milestone 1) with more milestones implied; NATO ACT is moving conformance from an annual event to continuous INSPECT checks; NSA's April 2026 guideline anchored ACP-240/ZTDF on the FVEY side; DISA targets a data-centric MPE by 2027; DIANA and the Rapid Adoption Action Plan (2025-06-25) opened faster allied on-ramps. These make the standards matter more, but they also show the requirement owners (ACT, NCIA, NSA/Virtru) are solving the conformance layer themselves.
killer_risk: There is no buyer for a standalone linter/simulator: NATO ACT owns conformance (INSPECT/CWIX) and gives it to affiliates for free, NCIA buys labelling as COTS from established vendors with IV&V bundled, vendors already hold the libraries, and the residual demand (CWIX preparation, DCS readiness) is already served by consultancies at a scale that cannot support a venture.

allied_extension: This gap only exists in allied form - it is already NATO-first. Allies supply the standards, the venue (CWIX/TIDE), the only dated budget line (NCIA DCS MS1) and the eligible on-ramps (DIANA, Bundeswehr channels) for a German-led team. But the allied market is also where the incumbents (Isode, Fortra, archTIS, Systematic) and the government harness (INSPECT) live, and national DCS budgets are small and fragmented; the U.S. extension (MPE/CIE, NGC2) was killed in the parent cards and remains closed to this cap table. Allied framing makes it legally feasible, not venture-scale.
